answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors verify fraud or duplicate control. A velvet onboarding flow may make each agent a mirror of a human credential, but the defense is the costly bond and credible, evidence-based slashing, not the credential alone. Creating a swarm then ties up capital in every identity, and an island of colluding agents risks losing all their bonds when caught.
